blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Looped transformers are a parameter-efficient alternative to standard transformers for language modeling. By reapplying the same layers across multiple loop steps, recent looped language models match the performance of non-looped models several times their size. While this architecture effectively reduces parameter memory, each loop step still stores its own keys and values, so the key-value (KV) cache grows linearly with the number of loop steps and becomes the main memory bottleneck. We observe that the KV cache of looped models is highly redundant along the loop axis and that the loop steps differ substantially in their sensitivity to quantization. Based on these observations, we propose $\textbf{LoopVQ}$, a KV cache vector quantization method for looped transformers that codes channels of multiple loop steps jointly, and fine-tunes the codebooks to match the output of the full-precision model. At 0.5 bits per element, LoopVQ outperforms existing KV cache vector quantization methods for standard LLMs on general, long chain-of-thought reasoning, and long-context retrieval tasks with Ouro and Huginn models. Its design is orthogonal to these methods, and combined with TaSQ, it retains much of the BF16 accuracy even at 0.25 bits per element. We also implement LoopVQ in SGLang, where it nearly halves the decode latency at a 32K-token context and raises the peak serving throughput by up to $4.3\times$ and $6.1\times$ on the 1.4B and 2.6B Ouro models compared to the BF16 baseline.

discarding any tokens. It has been widely studied for standard

These methods can also be applied to looped models, but they do not exploit the redundancy of
the cache across loop steps, and below one bit per element they lose much of their accuracy
(Figure b).

blocks.en: 6.2 Reasoning stability
blocks.zh: 6.2 合理稳定

blocks.en:

blocks.en:
When evaluating quantization methods, efficiency is usually measured as throughput or latency per generated token ignoring how many
tokens are needed to reach an answer. Compression errors can lengthen reasoning or keep it from terminating, significantly wasting computation and decoding time ( Liu et al., 2025 ; Cheong et al., 2026a ) . On GPQA-Diamond, CQ and TaSQ exhaust the
32K-token budget on most problems and generate about twice as many tokens as BF16, whereas LoopVQ
and TaSQ+LoopVQ follow the length distribution of BF16 (Figure 10 ). As a result, the throughput gains of LoopVQ
(Section 5.3 ) carry over to the time needed to answer.
Appendix D.4 extends this analysis, including early termination, to both models and bitwidths.

在评估量化方法时,通常以每个生成的符号的吞吐量或耐用度来衡量效率,而忽略了多少个
获得答案需要指示。 压缩错误可以延长推理时间或避免其终止、大量浪费计算和解码时间(Liu等,2025;Cheong等,2026a)。
32K-按键预算处理大多数问题,产生比BF16多大约两倍的代币,而LoopVQ
和 TaSQQLOOPVQ 遵循 BF16 的长度分布(图10.). 因此,LoopVQ的通量收益
(第5.3节)继续到答复所需的时间。
附录D.4将这一分析,包括早期终止,扩展至模型和比特width两种.

blocks.en: 7 Related work
blocks.zh: 7 相关工作

blocks.en:
Weight quantization methods for LLMs include scalar quantization with error compensation or
activation-aware scaling Frantar et al. (2022) ; Lin et al. (2024) , joint quantization of weights and
activations Xiao et al. (2023) ; Ashkboos et al. (2024) , and vector quantization with
codebooks Tseng et al. (2024) ; Egiazarian et al. (2024) . For the KV cache, scalar methods quantize keys
and values per channel or per token Liu et al. (2024) ; Hooper et al. (2024) ; Ashkboos et al. (2024) , and
vector quantization methods code groups of channels jointly Zhang et al. (2024) ; Cheong et al. (2026b) ; Son et al. (2026) .
These methods target non-looped models, where each layer writes one cache, and quantize the caches
of different layers independently.

激活 Xiao等人(2023年);Ashkboos等人(2024年),以及矢量定量与
代码簿 Tseng等 (2024年); Egiazarian等 (2024年). 对于 KV 缓存, Scalar 方法将密钥定量
每个频道或每个符号的值 刘等 (2024年); Hooper等 (2024年); Ashkboos等 (2024年),和
矢量量化方法 : 张等 (2024年); 程等 (2026年b); 宋等 (2026年).
这些方法针对非擦洗模型,其中每层写一个缓存,并将缓存量化
不同层的独立。

blocks.en:
The recurrence of looped transformers has motivated quantization methods tailored to it. LoopQ Fang et al. (2026) , LoopQuant Zhao et al. (2026) , and
Loopy Li et al. (2026) quantize the weights and activations of the shared block, accounting for
the distribution shift and error accumulation across loop steps. For the KV cache, which dominates
the memory of a looped model (Figure a), FlashLoop Yang and Liu (2026) and
ResidualQuant Kim et al. (2026) apply scalar quantization at 2 to 4 bits per
element. LoopVQ instead applies vector quantization along the loop axis to a pretrained
model, so that one index codes several loop steps, and compresses the KV cache below one bit per
element.

blocks.en: 8 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 8 结论

blocks.en:
We presented LoopVQ, a KV cache quantization method for looped transformers. LoopVQ groups
channels of multiple loop steps into a sub-vector that shares one index, and fine-tunes the
codebooks to match the output of the full-precision model, accounting for the different
quantization sensitivities of the loop steps. We showed that, at 0.5 and 0.25 bits
per element, LoopVQ outperforms existing vector quantization methods on general, reasoning, and
long-context benchmarks, and that our SGLang implementation reduces the decode latency and raises
the serving throughput over the BF16 baseline. The appendix
provides further analysis of the fine-tuning objective, implementation and kernel optimization details, and additional experiment results.

blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
Our efficiency evaluation compares LoopVQ with BF16 serving in SGLang and does not include the
baseline quantization methods. The serving efficiency of each method depends on kernels optimized
for its own cache format, and it is difficult to determine a comparable level of optimization for
every method. To avoid a comparison biased toward the method we optimized most, we compare against
BF16 serving, which SGLang already supports with highly optimized kernels.

我们的效率评价将LoopVQ与在SGLang服务的BF16相比较,不包括
基线量化方法。 每个方法的服务效率取决于内核优化
的缓存格式,很难确定可比较的优化水平
每一个方法。 为了避免偏向于我们最优化的方法,我们比较
BF16服务,SGLang已经以高度优化的内核支持.

blocks.en:
We also do not compare accuracy with FlashLoop Yang and Liu (2026) and
ResidualQuant Kim et al. (2026) , the existing KV cache quantization methods for looped
transformers. Both apply scalar quantization, which stores at least one bit per element and cannot
reach the sub-1-bit regime that LoopVQ targets. They are designed for 2 to 4 bits per element and
do not specify a configuration for lower bitwidths, so they cannot be compared with LoopVQ at
matched bitwidths.

blocks.en: Appendix C Optimizing pre-RoPE vector quantization serving efficiency
blocks.zh: 附录C 优化 ROPE 向量定量前服务效率

blocks.en:
LoopVQ, like CQ and TaSQ, quantizes keys before the rotary embedding (RoPE)
(Section 2 ), since RoPE rotates the same key differently at every position and
would spread the keys of one channel group over many more codebook entries. The decode attention
kernel then has to apply RoPE to every reconstructed key (Algorithm 1 ), which requires the
cosine and sine of D / 2 D/2 frequencies at the position of each cached token. Evaluating them in the
kernel adds transcendental operations for every token and frequency, so the kernel reads them from
a table precomputed for all positions, one row of D D values per position.

With one request per thread block, every block reads the table row of each token it attends to,
and the blocks of different requests read the same rows again. At large batch sizes these reads

index in the sequence, the rows needed by two requests coincide wherever both requests have a
token. The kernel assigns two requests to each thread block and cuts both into splits at
the same boundaries, sized by the longer request, so that one load of a table row serves the
tokens of both requests at the same index. The two requests also share the codebook slices ℬ t k \mathcal{B}^{k}_{t} and ℬ t v \mathcal{B}^{v}_{t} staged in shared memory, which halves the codebook loads per
request. The shared-memory buffers of each request are halved accordingly, so a block uses the same
shared memory as with one request. Each lane further handles the two channel groups that share the
same frequencies, so that it loads their cosines and sines with single vector loads. At batch size 1
the kernel processes one request per block.

blocks.en:
Figure 15 breaks down the GPU time by kernel type, measured with the PyTorch
profiler under the settings of Section 5.3 . During decoding, the linear layers
take the same time in all methods, and the difference comes from attention. With BF16, attention
grows with the context length and accounts for most of the decode time at 32K tokens, whereas
with LoopVQ it stays below the time of the linear layers. At batch size 16, attention takes
1.87 ms per generated token with BF16 and 0.63 and 0.54 ms with LoopVQ at 0.5 and 0.25 bit.
Encoding takes under 1% of the decode time and 5 to 7% of the prefill time.

blocks.en:
We also evaluate the base models on the 16 English tasks of LongBench ( Bai et al., 2023 ) ,
using the official prompts and metrics, greedy decoding, and prompts truncated in the middle to
64K tokens. As in the other long-context experiments, 64 sink and 256 recent tokens are kept in
bf16. CQ and TaSQ fall 7 to 13 points below the BF16 average (Table 6 ).
LoopVQ outperforms both baselines on average in every setting, and TaSQ+LoopVQ comes within
1.5 points of BF16 at 0.5 bit and achieves the highest average at both bitwidths.
